sources.headline: Jemima Goldsmith says ex-partner Russell Brand physically assaulted her
sources.text:
Jemima Goldsmith has said Russell Brand physically assaulted her and she accused him of “violence, coercive control and abuse”.The 52-year-old TV producer said she has always been “strongly and unequivocally” on the side of Brand’s victims as she opened up about her own “painful” experience with her former partner in a social media post on Monday.Shortly after Brand was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison, Goldsmith posted on X: “I am in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand’s trial, told their stories, testified and ensured justice was done.“I have had my own personal experience of his violence, coercive control and abuse. I had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident. I chose not to press charges at the time and not to go public with this, as I was worried about the impact of the press attention on my then teenage children.“I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014. Whilst my pain in relation to this pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact.”On Thursday, Brand was found guilty of raping a fan and sexually assaulting three women in separate incidents between 2004 and 2009. He was cleared of two further charges of rape and one of attempted indecent assault.Goldsmith, known professionally as Jemima Khan, is reported to have been in a relationship with Brand for a year from around September 2013. On X, Goldsmith said she had assisted the journalists who had exposed Brand in a Channel 4 Dispatches documentary and in reports in the Times and Sunday Times in 2023.“I also undertook to testify in court to his abusiveness, if the newspaper that published the victims’ accounts were ever to be sued,” she said.Goldsmith made the comments in light of renewed press reporting about a harassment injunction that she and Brand had taken out against a woman named Szilvia Berki in 2014.Goldsmith, who married former Pakistan cricket captain Imran Khan in 1995, said the online commentary and media reporting about the injunction had presented “an untrue narrative” and opened her up to “vile hatred and abuse online”.Berki had made allegations against Brand to the police after she had been booked to give him a massage at Goldsmith’s home in June 2014. It is understood the police found there was no case to answer.“I was present the whole time he was with her, and I did not see anything untoward, despite the fact that he was later found guilty of sexually assaulting other women and he later physically assaulted me. If I saw any man abuse any woman under any circumstances, I would do my utmost to stop them, without hesitation,” Goldsmith said in her statement.Goldsmith alleged that a series of “untrue stories” appeared in the tabloid press and that Berki embarked on a campaign of “threatening abuse online and in emails”. The Guardian has not been able to reach Berki.Brand and Goldsmith applied for a harassment injunction against Berki.The injunction was granted by the high court judge and former leading counsel in the Leveson inquiry Mr Justice Jay. It was brought to light by the non-profit campaigning thinktank Tax Policy Associates, founded by the former tax lawyer Dan Neidle, after Brand’s conviction.
This article was amended on 9 November 2026 to clarify the circumstances of the injunction.

sources.headline: Moment judge sentences Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault
sources.text:
Updated: 9 November 2026 - 16:51 GMT+1
British comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and 6 months in prison for rape and sexual assault.
The 50-year-old was convicted last week by a jury at London's Southwark Crown Court of one count of rape and three sexual assaults against four women between 2004 and 2009.
Judge Joel Bennathan handed down the sentence on Monday, with Brand to serve two-thirds of the term before being released on licence.
He will also be subject to indefinite notification requirements under the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

sources.headline: British comedian Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sexual assault
sources.text:
This is a court artist sketch by Elizabeth Cook of Russell Brand in the dock at Southwark Crown Court, in London, on Nov. 5.
Elizabeth Cook/PA/AP
hide caption
Elizabeth Cook/PA/AP
Russell Brand, the raunchy, irreverent British comedian who became a celebrity darling in the early 2000s, has been sentenced to over 10 years in prison after being found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. "The total sentence is one of ten years, six months," said Judge Justice Bennathan on handing down the sentence at Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday. Brand, 51, was a career chameleon who went from stand-up comic and MTV host to a political analyst esteemed by Britain's left, only to become a conspiracy theorist and Christian convert beloved by the U.S. right.
But critics of Brand said there was always a clear thread of misogyny running through his comedy routines, and that his mistreatment of women had been an open secret for decades. Over the past four weeks, six women testified against the comedian in court in London, in a trial that garnered massive media attention. A jury found Brand guilty last week on four of the seven counts against him. He was found guilty of raping a woman he'd met at one of his shows in 2009 and of sexually assaulting three women — at a bar, a radio station and a TV studio — between 2004 and 2009. Brand denies all charges and said he never had non-consensual sex. Before the judge handed down the sentence, four of the women who brought the case against Brand gave victim impact statements to the court. Three of the statements were read out by the prosecution, while one woman appeared in court behind a curtain to read her own. None of the women have been publicly named and the trial was not televised. Victim impact statements read The prosecution read out an impact statement from the one complainant, who Brand was found guilty of anally raping at his home in 2009. In her statement she said: "It's something I carry with me every day and it often feels never-ending."
"I doubt my ability to make good decisions and no longer trust my instinct in the way I did," her statement said, adding that because of Brand's fame she didn't think she'd be believed if she reported him.
Russell Brand is seen on stage during a tribute for Amy Winehouse at the MTV Video Music Awards on Sunday Aug. 28, 2011, in Los Angeles.
Matt Sayles/AP
hide caption
Matt Sayles/AP
Another complainant, who Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting at a bar in 2004 when he grabbed her breasts, said the confusion of what she "should" or "could" do had stayed with her for over 20 years. The complainant, who spoke in person from behind a curtain in the courtroom, said she felt "physically sick" seeing Brand in the press afterwards as his fame rose. Another of Brand's victims, who he was found guilty of sexually assaulting in 2005, said the assault had "a lasting impact on her life" and that over the years "hearing his voice on television or seeing his image has made me jump." A fourth woman, who Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting when they worked together at a TV studio, said she was badly affected and afterwards felt her working environment was unsafe. Brand holds rosary and prays British media who were in the court for the sentencing said Brand, who had spent the weekend in prison, was in the suit he was convicted in on Thursday and sat holding a set of white rosary beads as the victim statements were read. Brand's wife Laura, who had supported him throughout the case, was in court, as was his father. After the victim statements, the defense and prosecution teams had the opportunity to make their last statements. The prosecution called for a long sentence, saying there were aggravating circumstances in the anal rape case, such as Brand removing a condom. The defence meanwhile said Brand was "a fundamentally different person" from who he was at the time of the crimes.
After considering the victim impact statements and those by the defence and prosecution, the judge handed down the sentence live on camera. In his remarks, he said Brand had become "a sexual predator" and paused "to pay tribute to the determination and bravery" of the women who'd come forward. He then ordered Brand to be taken down to the cells.

Published: 10:54pm, 9 Nov 2026Updated: 7:43am, 10 Nov 2026

British comedian and television star Russell Brand was on Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him.

Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm.

“About 20 years ago Russell Brand, you were becoming famous, you were clever, and in many people’s eyes you were funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator,” he said.

The judge said Brand’s status protected him until he was exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police.

Bennathan paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women, adding Brand had repeatedly acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”.

Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher (centre) is helped into a car after her husband’s sentencing in London on Monday. Photo: AFP

Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced.

Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK”, before being led down to the cells.

The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009.

Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen.

She said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004.

“For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court.

A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him.

“His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said.

Ronald Brand, the father of Russell Brand, outside Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday. Photo: PA Wire / dpa

The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims.

Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. But he is facing further investigations after London police revealed rape allegations by two more women.

From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous prime time show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian’s obsession with sex and his no-holds barred delivery contributed to his notoriety.

Brand denied the charges but he admitted to being “extremely promiscuous” and using his fame to “facilitate sexual access”.

Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London, in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25.

He had his own radio show at the BBC, which last week apologised for the “culture and failings” when Brand worked there between 2006 and 2008.

Brand left the BBC after leaving sexually explicit messages on a well-known actor’s answering machine about having slept with the actor’s granddaughter.

Brand and US singer Katy Perry at the premiere of the film Get Him to the Greek in Los Angeles in May 2010. Photo: AFP

After a brief marriage in 2010 to US pop star Katy Perry, Brand made a foray into Hollywood, starring in films Forgetting Sarah Marshall, Get Him to the Greek and Arthur.

The court found Brand guilty of sexual assaults against an MTV worker, a Channel 4 worker and a Capital Radio employee, as well as raping a fan.

The organisations that propped up Brand for years are now facing questions about how he continued for so long.

British culture minister Lisa Nandy said men in power were still exploiting women in the media industry, saying his case was a “wake-up call”.

Speaking outside court, the lead detective in the case Andy Furphy said the sentence was a “milestone” that had seen Brand finally “held accountable for his crimes”.

And he praised the “immense bravery, dignity and resilience” of the victims who had had “to revisit deeply traumatic experiences”.

As he left court, Brand’s father Ron Brand told reporters his son had been a “victim” and that both Russell and his daughter-in-law would be all right.

“Yeah, he’s strong, he’s strong,” he said, when asked how his son would cope in jail, adding “she’s strong as well”, referring to Laura.

By
Lucia I Suarez Sang

Updated on: November 9, 2026 / 7:38 PM EST
/ CBS News
Add CBS News on Google
Disgraced actor Russell Brand was sentenced Monday to 10 and a half years in prison for raping a woman in 2009 and sexually assaulting three others.The disgraced British television personality and Hollywood actor was convicted last week on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, but acquitted on two other counts of rape and an attempted indecent assault charge.A jury of eight men and four women in Southwark Crown Court, in South London, found Brand guilty of groping a woman's breasts at a London bar in 2004, sexually assaulting a woman at a London radio station in 2004 and 2005, and raping a woman at his west London home in 2009.The judge, Joel Bennathan, called Brand a "sexual predator" in his sentencing remarks, saying he displayed "staggering arrogance" and believed that "fame meant you could act ⁠how you liked, when you liked."For the rape he was sentenced to nine years, plus 18 months for the sexual assaults. Brand is expected to serve at least seven years in prison, and the rest of his sentence under heavy restrictions, such as wearing a tag.Six women made the allegations against him, spanning from 1999 to 2009.
Russell Brand outside Southwark Crown Court in London on Nov. 4, 2026.
James Manning/PA Images via Getty Images
Before the sentencing Monday, victim impact statements from the women involved in Brand's crimes were read out in court, three by the prosecutor and one by one of the women, who was hidden from everyone but the judge by a screen.
"I've been in shock and turmoil for years. I was extremely upset and traumatized. I didn't have any respect for myself," the woman reading her statement said, according to CBS News partner network BBC."I was thinking I was damaged goods - scared of giving off signals that could be taken the wrong way."Another statement, read out by the prosecutor, called Brand "a sexual predator who has no remorse … I just hope he is not allowed to hurt any more women."A third statement, from the woman who Brand was convicted of raping in 2009, said she "struggled to sleep and eat" and "cope with my emotions" after the attack.
Before the sentence was announced, Brand's lawyer Ian Winter KC said his client was a "fundamentally different person today" compared to when the rape took place 17 years ago. He called the rape a "momentary total failure to respect [the woman's] consent."Brand was denied bail after the conviction and remained in custody ahead of Monday's sentencing, as the London judge rejected his request to be released on bail to spend time with his wife and children before Monday's hearing."I regret the hardship caused to the children, of course," judge Bennathan said of his decision Thursday, according to the BBC. "But the hardship has been caused by serious criminal offending by their father."Following the verdicts being handed down last week, the BBC reported that police were investigating Brand over additional rape allegations made by two women — one of whom was 16 years old at the time of the alleged incident. The head of London's Metropolitan Police said Friday that he "wouldn't be surprised ‌if many ⁠more [women] came forward."When the guilty verdict was read out, Brand closed his eyes. When bail was denied he said, "I'm good, I'm good, I'm good," before being led away. His lawyers argued that the victims' cases were weakened by the fact they had only gone to the police years after the encounters. Brand, who had pleaded not guilty to all charges, suggested the claims were part of a coordinated attack on his character due to his prominence as an online wellness influencer and political commentator.
He admitted to leading a promiscuous life and being obsessed with sex as a young man, but claimed he never forced anyone to do anything against their will. During the trial, a prosecutor described Brand as a ruthless and manipulative sexual predator.
